world.title: 20,000 march in Madrid after evicted pensioner Maricarmen dies
world.summary: About 20,000 people marched through central Madrid on Thursday to remember María del Carmen Abascal, known as Maricarmen, whose eviction had become a focus of protests over Spain’s housing crisis. Police put the Madrid crowd at at least 20,000; commemorative marches also took place in other Spanish cities. The march we
world.content: About 20,000 people marched through central Madrid on Thursday to remember María del Carmen Abascal, known as Maricarmen, whose eviction had become a focus of protests over Spain’s housing crisis. Police put the Madrid crowd at at least 20,000; commemorative marches also took place in other Spanish cities. The march went from a protest camp in Puerta del Sol to Abascal’s former home, where mourners left flowers, candles and notes. Conservatives rejected calls for tributes in regional and national legislatures, while left-leaning lawmakers held their own observances. Unions have called a nationwide strike for Nov. 11, and Spain is scheduled to hold a general election on Nov. 29. Rents have risen an average of 84% over the past decade, while the Bank of Spain has estimated a housing shortfall of about 750,000 homes.
world.image_alt: 20,000 march in Madrid after evicted pensioner Maricarmen dies

world.title: Nobel committee prepares to announce 2026 Peace Prize amid Trump lobbying
world.summary: The Norwegian Nobel Committee is due to announce the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize winner in Oslo on Friday, choosing from 287 nominations: 208 individuals and 79 organizations. The Peace Prize is the only Nobel announced in Oslo. The ceremony is scheduled for Dec. 10, and this year’s award is worth 12 million Swedish kronor,
world.content: The Norwegian Nobel Committee is due to announce the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize winner in Oslo on Friday, choosing from 287 nominations: 208 individuals and 79 organizations. The Peace Prize is the only Nobel announced in Oslo. The ceremony is scheduled for Dec. 10, and this year’s award is worth 12 million Swedish kronor, about $1.2 million. Names publicly discussed as possible recipients include Sudan’s Emergency Response Rooms, Ukrainian children’s rights advocate Mykola Kuleba, Save the Children, the Committee to Protect Journalists and Pope Leo XIV. These are expert predictions, not an official shortlist: the committee does not publish the names under consideration. President Donald Trump has repeatedly said he deserves the award. On Wednesday, he said it would be a “great discredit” if the committee did not select him. Last year’s laureate, Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado, gave Trump her medal in January, but the committee says the award itself cannot be transferred. Analysts have questioned Trump’s prospects, citing the U.S. war with Iran and the prize’s peace criteria.
world.image_alt: Nobel committee prepares to announce 2026 Peace Prize amid Trump lobbying

world.title: Trump envoys take Ukraine peace proposals to Miami talks with Kyiv
world.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are due to meet Ukrainian negotiators in Miami on Oct. 9 and 10, with European officials invited, to discuss new proposals to end Russia’s war in Ukraine. The proposals were developed through recent U.S. contacts with both Moscow and Kyiv, and Washing
world.content: U.S. President Donald Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are due to meet Ukrainian negotiators in Miami on Oct. 9 and 10, with European officials invited, to discuss new proposals to end Russia’s war in Ukraine. The proposals were developed through recent U.S. contacts with both Moscow and Kyiv, and Washington is seeking a unified proposal. The agenda is expected to include security guarantees for Ukraine and a postwar economic plan. Reports also say a partial ceasefire covering attacks on energy infrastructure and grain shipping is under consideration. Witkoff and Kushner may travel to Moscow later this month to discuss the proposals with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Witkoff and Kushner briefed Trump on the latest proposals on Oct. 8. Washington is pressing for progress before winter and the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russian strikes killed 78 people and wounded 215 across Ukraine over the previous two days.
world.image_alt: Trump envoys take Ukraine peace proposals to Miami talks with Kyiv

world.title: Russian glide bomb kills 30 near buses in Ukraine
world.summary: A Russian glide bomb struck near two passenger buses in Kramatorsk, eastern Ukraine, killing at least 30 people, Ukrainian officials said Thursday. The strike wounded 18 people, and shelling killed three more in nearby Bilenke, officials said. Ukraine accused Russia of deliberately striking civilians; Moscow had not co
world.content: A Russian glide bomb struck near two passenger buses in Kramatorsk, eastern Ukraine, killing at least 30 people, Ukrainian officials said Thursday. The strike wounded 18 people, and shelling killed three more in nearby Bilenke, officials said. Ukraine accused Russia of deliberately striking civilians; Moscow had not commented on the attack by Thursday. Kramatorsk and neighbouring Sloviansk are among the last major cities in northern Donetsk under Ukrainian control and form part of the region’s so-called fortress belt. The attack came a day after a Russian missile hit an apartment block in Pryluky, killing 22 people, including five children, and wounding at least 54. The United Nations said civilian deaths in Ukraine through August 2026 had exceeded the total for all of 2025. After visiting Pryluky, British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband announced new sanctions on Russia. Zelensky said Ukrainian representatives would meet President Donald Trump’s envoys in the United States on Friday and Saturday to discuss air defences.
world.image_alt: Russian glide bomb kills 30 near buses in Ukraine

world.title: US suspends eight technology firms from PERM green-card program
world.summary: The Trump administration on Oct. 8 suspended Microsoft, Adobe and six other technology and outsourcing companies from the PERM labor-certification process, barring new and pending applications involving them. The Labor Department said the move followed federal investigations into alleged misuse of the process, which em
world.content: The Trump administration on Oct. 8 suspended Microsoft, Adobe and six other technology and outsourcing companies from the PERM labor-certification process, barring new and pending applications involving them. The Labor Department said the move followed federal investigations into alleged misuse of the process, which employers must complete before sponsoring most workers for employment-based green cards. The action does not cancel employees’ existing H-1B visas, but it blocks a common route from temporary work status to permanent residency. Vice President JD Vance singled out Microsoft, alleging it laid off 6,000 U.S. workers in 2025 while receiving more than 6,000 H-1B approvals and filing thousands of PERM applications. Microsoft said most of its U.S. employees are Americans and that it would provide the administration with further information. The administration also announced investigations into nine universities over alleged misuse of J-1 exchange-visitor visas; the Labor Department inspector general said subpoenas had been served. Vance said the company suspensions would remain in place “as long as it needs to”.
world.image_alt: US suspends eight technology firms from PERM green-card program

world.title: Labour retains Starmer
world.summary: Labour candidate Sagal Abdi-Wali won the Holborn and St Pancras by-election in London, defeating Green Party leader Zack Polanski and retaining the seat vacated by former Prime Minister Keir Starmer. Abdi-Wali received 12,292 votes to Polanski’s 8,928, a majority of 3,364. Turnout was 38.7%, the lowest in an English by
world.content: Labour candidate Sagal Abdi-Wali won the Holborn and St Pancras by-election in London, defeating Green Party leader Zack Polanski and retaining the seat vacated by former Prime Minister Keir Starmer. Abdi-Wali received 12,292 votes to Polanski’s 8,928, a majority of 3,364. Turnout was 38.7%, the lowest in an English by-election during this parliament. The victory came in Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s first major electoral test. The Greens had targeted the traditionally Labour seat, seeking support from voters who had moved left during Starmer’s premiership. Polanski said voters told him they wanted to give Burnham a chance. The contest followed a Green Party conference vote to adopt a motion describing Zionism as racism. Four of the party’s five MPs opposed the decision, which also drew criticism within the party. Polanski said he would remain leader; under party rules, he faces a scheduled leadership election next summer.

world.title: USS Abraham Lincoln returns after 265 consecutive days at sea
world.summary: The USS Abraham Lincoln returned to its San Diego-area home port on Oct. 8 after a 321-day deployment supporting U.S. operations in the Iran war, including a record 265 consecutive days at sea without a port call. Families welcomed sailors after nearly a year apart, including fathers meeting babies born during the depl
world.content: The USS Abraham Lincoln returned to its San Diego-area home port on Oct. 8 after a 321-day deployment supporting U.S. operations in the Iran war, including a record 265 consecutive days at sea without a port call. Families welcomed sailors after nearly a year apart, including fathers meeting babies born during the deployment. The carrier left California for the Pacific in November 2025 and was redirected to the Middle East after the war began. The deployment drew scrutiny over reports of shortages of food and hygiene supplies, plumbing problems and declining crew mental health. The Navy acknowledged that eight people in the strike group attempted suicide. Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao said limited opportunities to resupply temporarily reduced meal choices, while the ship’s commander said the crew had access to four meals a day. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth visited the carrier on Wednesday and presented its crew with the Presidential Unit Citation. He rejected portrayals of the ship as a sign of dysfunction. Crew families and Democratic lawmakers had raised concerns for months before the carrier’s return.
world.image_alt: USS Abraham Lincoln returns after 265 consecutive days at sea

world.title: France pledges 3,000 substitute teachers as student protests persist
world.summary: Student-led demonstrations across France drew 71,500 people on Thursday, Oct. 8, and police detained more than 500, the Interior Ministry said. In Paris, police used tear gas and water cannon and charged protesters near the Bastille after clashes. Demonstrations elsewhere were largely peaceful, though some turned viole
world.content: Student-led demonstrations across France drew 71,500 people on Thursday, Oct. 8, and police detained more than 500, the Interior Ministry said. In Paris, police used tear gas and water cannon and charged protesters near the Bastille after clashes. Demonstrations elsewhere were largely peaceful, though some turned violent. Education Minister Édouard Geffray said the government would send 3,000 substitute teachers to schools with acute shortages between Friday and Tuesday. He also said several hundred teachers could be recruited, while the government reviews long school days and the university admissions platform Parcoursup. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has promised proposals by the end of October but has not detailed them. Students cite teacher shortages, deteriorating school buildings and demanding schedules. Student representatives said Thursday’s meeting with the minister had not produced enough concrete commitments, and unions called for another national day of action on Tuesday, Oct. 13.
world.image_alt: France pledges 3,000 substitute teachers as student protests persist

business.title: French bond selloff pushes yields above 5% as European bank shares fall
business.summary: French government bonds have come under renewed pressure, with the 10-year yield briefly exceeding 5% last week for the first time since 2002 and remaining near 4.9% on Thursday. The risk premium investors demand over German 10-year debt also reached its highest level since 2011 as concerns about France’s deficit, poli
business.content: French government bonds have come under renewed pressure, with the 10-year yield briefly exceeding 5% last week for the first time since 2002 and remaining near 4.9% on Thursday. The risk premium investors demand over German 10-year debt also reached its highest level since 2011 as concerns about France’s deficit, political deadlock and the 2027 presidential election intensified. Investors doubt France can pass budget changes and reduce its deficit as successive governments struggle to get austerity measures through a divided parliament. European bank shares fell sharply, while bond yields also rose in Italy, Germany and the United Kingdom. Some asset managers have begun buying eurozone bonds, saying fears of a crisis comparable to the previous eurozone debt turmoil are overstated. French officials say the country can still attract investors and have kept its debt-issuance strategy unchanged. European Central Bank officials say current conditions do not justify intervention. Its bond-buying backstop is intended for unjustified, disorderly market moves and requires fiscal-policy conditions to be met.
business.image_alt: French bond selloff pushes yields above 5% as European bank shares fall

business.title: Fed governor Waller signals October pause, still sees further hikes
business.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said another interest-rate increase is needed to curb inflation but left the timing open, casting doubt on a hike at the Fed’s October meeting. Waller said the central bank need not raise rates at consecutive meetings; a New York Times report said a further increase was unlik
business.content: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said another interest-rate increase is needed to curb inflation but left the timing open, casting doubt on a hike at the Fed’s October meeting. Waller said the central bank need not raise rates at consecutive meetings; a New York Times report said a further increase was unlikely until year-end. Minutes from the Fed’s September meeting showed most officials viewed another increase by year-end as appropriate, while saying future decisions would depend on incoming data. The minutes also recorded concerns that energy costs and other price pressures could spread through the economy. Investors were pricing in more than an 80% chance the Fed would hold rates at its October meeting, according to market data cited by Capital Spectator.
business.image_alt: Fed governor Waller signals October pause, still sees further hikes

business.title: NFL asks Supreme Court to put sports prediction markets under state gambling rules
business.summary: The NFL urged the U.S. Supreme Court on Thursday to decide whether states or the federal government should regulate sports prediction markets, arguing that contracts tied to game outcomes are gambling rather than financial swaps. The league filed a brief supporting New Jersey’s request for review and backed appellate r
business.content: The NFL urged the U.S. Supreme Court on Thursday to decide whether states or the federal government should regulate sports prediction markets, arguing that contracts tied to game outcomes are gambling rather than financial swaps. The league filed a brief supporting New Jersey’s request for review and backed appellate rulings allowing states to enforce gambling laws. Another appeals court ruled for Kalshi, leaving the courts divided. The NFL says the uncertainty threatens consumer protection and game integrity as trading in contracts tied to its games grows. It cited about $1.8 billion in NFL-related contracts traded on the season’s opening Sunday, out of $3.3 billion in total prediction-market volume that day. Kalshi says the CFTC is actively policing these markets, while Polymarket says it is working toward a federal framework. The Supreme Court has not agreed to hear the case; the NFL asked it to act before another season passes.
business.image_alt: NFL asks Supreme Court to put sports prediction markets under state gambling rules

business.title: Pimco warns US 10-year Treasury yield could reach 6%
business.summary: Pimco chief investment officer Dan Ivascyn said the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield could rise to 6%—a level not seen since 2000—as investors unwind losing bond positions after weeks of selling. He said a further sharp rise was possible, with the yield already at its highest level in more than two decades. Higher borrowing
business.content: Pimco chief investment officer Dan Ivascyn said the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield could rise to 6%—a level not seen since 2000—as investors unwind losing bond positions after weeks of selling. He said a further sharp rise was possible, with the yield already at its highest level in more than two decades. Higher borrowing costs could weigh on stocks and corporate bonds, Firstpost reported, citing rising oil prices, inflation risks and growing U.S. debt as drivers of the bond-market move. David Zervos, a new adviser to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, said yields were “really, really high” but could fall soon; the 10-year and 30-year yields had reached 24-year highs in recent days.
business.image_alt: Pimco warns US 10-year Treasury yield could reach 6%

business.title: OpenAI revenue estimate falls $20 billion short, unsettling AI shares
business.summary: OpenAI told financial backers its annualized revenue was nearing $50 billion at the end of September, about $20 billion below the roughly $70 billion figure previously circulated to investors. The figure is a revenue run rate, not actual full-year revenue. The gap partly reflects differences in accounting for sales thr
business.content: OpenAI told financial backers its annualized revenue was nearing $50 billion at the end of September, about $20 billion below the roughly $70 billion figure previously circulated to investors. The figure is a revenue run rate, not actual full-year revenue. The gap partly reflects differences in accounting for sales through cloud partners; the earlier estimate was adjusted to make OpenAI’s numbers more comparable with Anthropic’s. Technology shares fell after the disclosure on Oct. 8. The Nasdaq fell 1.25% and the Philadelphia semiconductor index dropped 3.39%; Nvidia fell 2.94%, Oracle 5.48% and cloud-computing provider CoreWeave 7.77%. OpenAI’s investor materials also showed that its revenue run rate grew 77% in the third quarter, while its enterprise revenue run rate increased 107%. Oracle’s capital spending rose to $28.5 billion in its latest quarter from $8.5 billion a year earlier. Firmus shelved a planned Australian IPO of up to $5.5 billion, citing volatile markets, and said it would consider private funding.
business.image_alt: OpenAI revenue estimate falls $20 billion short, unsettling AI shares

business.title: Trump auto-enrolls 60 million children, lifting accounts to 70 million
business.summary: President Donald Trump said the Treasury automatically enrolled about 60 million children in Trump Accounts on Oct. 1, bringing total enrollment to roughly 70 million, including accounts opened by families since the program launched July 4. The White House says deposits total more than $4.5 billion, including $1.3 bill
business.content: President Donald Trump said the Treasury automatically enrolled about 60 million children in Trump Accounts on Oct. 1, bringing total enrollment to roughly 70 million, including accounts opened by families since the program launched July 4. The White House says deposits total more than $4.5 billion, including $1.3 billion in federal seed money, $2.6 billion in philanthropic contributions and more than $600 million from families and friends. Automatic enrollment alone does not mean an account has been claimed or its seed payment secured: parents or guardians must verify their identity and relationship to the child through the Trump Accounts app. Children born from 2025 through 2028 qualify for a one-time $1,000 federal deposit after an account is claimed; eligible children born from 2016 through 2024 may receive $250 from the Michael and Susan Dell Foundation. Funds are invested in accounts tracking large U.S. companies and generally cannot be accessed until the child turns 18.
business.image_alt: Trump auto-enrolls 60 million children, lifting accounts to 70 million

business.title: SpaceX agrees to acquire 800 MHz spectrum to challenge US wireless carriers
business.summary: SpaceX agreed to acquire up to 14 megahertz of paired 800 MHz spectrum from investment firm Grain Management for its planned US wireless carrier, Starlink Mobile. The low-band licenses are intended to help satellite signals reach phones inside buildings, complementing Starlink Mobile’s existing 2 GHz spectrum. The comp
business.content: SpaceX agreed to acquire up to 14 megahertz of paired 800 MHz spectrum from investment firm Grain Management for its planned US wireless carrier, Starlink Mobile. The low-band licenses are intended to help satellite signals reach phones inside buildings, complementing Starlink Mobile’s existing 2 GHz spectrum. The companies did not disclose financial terms, and the deal requires Federal Communications Commission approval. The FCC approved SpaceX’s deployment of 15,000 next-generation Starlink Mobile satellites earlier this week. SpaceX says the new constellation will connect directly to standard phones, while the acquired frequencies would provide indoor coverage. Shares of AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon fell in after-hours trading after the announcement, with reported declines ranging from roughly 5% to more than 7%. SpaceX plans to combine satellites with terrestrial infrastructure, but analysts say reliable urban coverage would require ground facilities and significant investment. The spectrum transaction awaits FCC clearance, and SpaceX’s separate $20 billion EchoStar spectrum deal is not expected to close until November 2027. The timing of a full retail mobile launch remains uncertain.
business.image_alt: SpaceX agrees to acquire 800 MHz spectrum to challenge US wireless carriers

business.title: PepsiCo cuts 2026 profit outlook as North American sales weaken
business.summary: PepsiCo lowered its 2026 adjusted earnings-per-share growth forecast to 2.5%–3.5% from 5%–7% after North American sales volumes remained weak. Third-quarter net revenue rose 5.6% to $25.27 billion. The company now expects full-year revenue growth of 6%, the top of its previous 4%–6% range. Frito-Lay snack volumes in No
business.content: PepsiCo lowered its 2026 adjusted earnings-per-share growth forecast to 2.5%–3.5% from 5%–7% after North American sales volumes remained weak. Third-quarter net revenue rose 5.6% to $25.27 billion. The company now expects full-year revenue growth of 6%, the top of its previous 4%–6% range. Frito-Lay snack volumes in North America were flat year over year, while beverage volumes fell 2%; international business helped lift global snack volumes. PepsiCo said it would step up innovation and marketing in North America and cut corporate costs. Some snack and drink prices are set to rise in the coming weeks.
business.image_alt: PepsiCo cuts 2026 profit outlook as North American sales weaken

science.title: Kīlauea’s 54 lava-fountaining episodes offer clues to eruption mechanics
science.summary: Kīlauea’s summit eruption has produced 54 episodes of lava fountaining inside Halemaʻumaʻu crater since it began in December 2024. Scientists are studying the repeated bursts to understand what drives them, drawing on more than a year of observations. Episodic lava fountaining is rare globally; before this eruption, Kī
science.content: Kīlauea’s summit eruption has produced 54 episodes of lava fountaining inside Halemaʻumaʻu crater since it began in December 2024. Scientists are studying the repeated bursts to understand what drives them, drawing on more than a year of observations. Episodic lava fountaining is rare globally; before this eruption, Kīlauea had only three recorded occurrences since 1823. Researchers using several methods may have ruled out one proposed explanation, Science News reported. Their study, published in Science, examines the continuing sequence.
science.image_alt: Kīlauea’s 54 lava-fountaining episodes offer clues to eruption mechanics

science.title: COP31 leaders press governments to turn climate pledges into action
science.summary: COP31 President Murat Kurum and other officials urged governments to accelerate climate action at pre-summit talks in Fiji, despite expectations that global warming will temporarily exceed 1.5C. After visiting Tuvalu, Kurum called the temperature limit a matter of survival for Pacific communities. A UN report published
science.content: COP31 President Murat Kurum and other officials urged governments to accelerate climate action at pre-summit talks in Fiji, despite expectations that global warming will temporarily exceed 1.5C. After visiting Tuvalu, Kurum called the temperature limit a matter of survival for Pacific communities. A UN report published in September said warming would exceed the threshold but could be brought back below it by the end of the century with stronger action. Ahead of COP31 in Antalya, African climate negotiators say governments must turn pledges into results on the ground. They are seeking predictable, grant-based finance for adaptation and adequate support for loss and damage. Australia has proposed a plan to improve access to climate funding for small island states and poorer countries, including an annual forum to track implementation.
science.image_alt: COP31 leaders press governments to turn climate pledges into action

science.title: Forecasters warn California faces unusually wet winter as El Niño strengthens
science.summary: California is preparing for heavy rain, coastal flooding, high surf and landslides this winter as an unusually strong El Niño develops in the Pacific. NOAA’s latest forecast puts the chance of a “very strong” event above 90% and the chance of a historic event at about 75%. Two climate-model runs point to a wetter-than-
science.content: California is preparing for heavy rain, coastal flooding, high surf and landslides this winter as an unusually strong El Niño develops in the Pacific. NOAA’s latest forecast puts the chance of a “very strong” event above 90% and the chance of a historic event at about 75%. Two climate-model runs point to a wetter-than-usual winter in California, with heavy rain potentially continuing into spring. El Niño may raise sea levels along California’s coast by about a foot, on top of the 8 to 12 inches of rise attributed to climate change over the past century. Storms could also trigger debris flows on recently burned hillsides. Gov. Gavin Newsom declared a state of emergency on Sept. 21 to mobilize preparations; local agencies are securing infrastructure and positioning emergency resources.
science.image_alt: Forecasters warn California faces unusually wet winter as El Niño strengthens

science.title: 1960 model’s infinite-population forecast fails as growth slows
science.summary: A population model published in 1960 projected that humanity would reach an effectively infinite population in 2026. Science revisited the prediction on Oct. 8 as population growth has slowed rather than followed that trajectory. The model extrapolated a rapid postwar increase that began to ease in the mid-1960s, accor
science.content: A population model published in 1960 projected that humanity would reach an effectively infinite population in 2026. Science revisited the prediction on Oct. 8 as population growth has slowed rather than followed that trajectory. The model extrapolated a rapid postwar increase that began to ease in the mid-1960s, according to Javier Birchenall of the University of California, Santa Barbara, whose Science article examines the failed forecast. Birchenall argues that projections can mistake temporary trends for permanent laws, a warning he also applies to forecasts about falling birth rates and artificial intelligence. Roberto Natalini of Italy’s National Research Council said mathematical models remain useful as warnings for decision-makers, even when their assumptions later change.
science.image_alt: 1960 model’s infinite-population forecast fails as growth slows

science.title: OpenAI releases 722 AI-written math papers claiming advances on 372 open problems
science.summary: OpenAI has published 722 mathematical research papers generated by an unreleased internal AI model, claiming full or partial solutions to 372 open problems in mathematics and theoretical computer science. The company said it tested the system on about 4,000 problems and that producing a result took an average of three
science.content: OpenAI has published 722 mathematical research papers generated by an unreleased internal AI model, claiming full or partial solutions to 372 open problems in mathematics and theoretical computer science. The company said it tested the system on about 4,000 problems and that producing a result took an average of three hours of computing time. The papers span fields including algebra, geometry and mathematical logic. The release does not establish 372 independently verified breakthroughs. Several results concern progress on famous questions such as the Riemann hypothesis and Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, but OpenAI’s work does not fully solve any Millennium Prize problem. Some proofs have been checked with Lean, while mathematicians are assessing whether the arguments are correct, understandable and genuinely novel. Researchers have welcomed potential advances while questioning the papers’ quality, their attribution to earlier human work and the burden of reviewing hundreds of results. OpenAI said it consulted mathematicians and will support workshops and academic events to help the community assess the work. Independent review is still underway.
science.image_alt: OpenAI releases 722 AI-written math papers claiming advances on 372 open problems

science.title: Daughter of Apollo software pioneer Margaret Hamilton recalls belated recognition
science.summary: Recent tributes to Margaret Hamilton have focused on the recognition she gained decades after her Apollo software work. Her daughter, Lauren Hamilton, said public attention surged around the 50th anniversary of Apollo 11 in 2019, bringing her mother from relative obscurity to wide recognition among people in her field.
science.content: Recent tributes to Margaret Hamilton have focused on the recognition she gained decades after her Apollo software work. Her daughter, Lauren Hamilton, said public attention surged around the 50th anniversary of Apollo 11 in 2019, bringing her mother from relative obscurity to wide recognition among people in her field. She described her mother as reserved and said Hamilton was pleased that her work was finally acknowledged. Software was treated as a “black box” during the Apollo era, before the discipline gained the professional standing it has today. Hamilton said her young team took the work seriously and had to solve problems no one had tackled before. She also encountered sexism, her daughter said, often responding with humor rather than confrontation. Hamilton's software design work beyond Apollo included methods intended to prevent errors and tools for specifying complete systems.
science.image_alt: Daughter of Apollo software pioneer Margaret Hamilton recalls belated recognition

science.title: Quantum researchers report new routes to entanglement across atoms and matter
science.summary: Researchers reported several distinct approaches to quantum entanglement, including a Science paper on high-fidelity entangling gates and nonlocal circuits using neutral atoms, and an experiment linking light to a levitated glass sphere at room temperature. Two new arXiv preprints describe separate proposals: cavity-me
science.content: Researchers reported several distinct approaches to quantum entanglement, including a Science paper on high-fidelity entangling gates and nonlocal circuits using neutral atoms, and an experiment linking light to a levitated glass sphere at room temperature. Two new arXiv preprints describe separate proposals: cavity-mediated squeezing in atomic ensembles intended to generate entanglement more than 100 times faster than typical experiments, and remote magnon entanglement controlled through cavities and coherent feedback. The papers address different systems, not a single shared experiment.
science.image_alt: Quantum researchers report new routes to entanglement across atoms and matter

science.title: Study links weakened jumping-gene control to faster aging in large dogs
science.summary: Large dogs show faster epigenetic aging than smaller dogs, researchers found in a study using 1,640 DNA methylation profiles from 894 dogs. The team’s epigenetic clock tracked biological aging and predicted mortality. In larger dogs, reduced methylation at transposable DNA elements was associated with size-related diff
science.content: Large dogs show faster epigenetic aging than smaller dogs, researchers found in a study using 1,640 DNA methylation profiles from 894 dogs. The team’s epigenetic clock tracked biological aging and predicted mortality. In larger dogs, reduced methylation at transposable DNA elements was associated with size-related differences in aging. These elements, sometimes called “jumping genes,” may become more active when methylation falls, potentially damaging other genes and contributing to inflammation. The researchers say the findings do not establish that transposon activity causes faster aging. They plan to develop more informative clocks as the Dog Aging Project enrolls more dogs and follows them for longer, with the aim of explaining more of the variation in dogs’ epigenetic ages.
science.image_alt: Study links weakened jumping-gene control to faster aging in large dogs

sports.title: Buccaneers beat Cowboys 24-16 for first win of season
sports.summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers beat the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 on Thursday night for their first win of the NFL season. Rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels led Tampa Bay with help from running back Bucky Irving. Dallas had been favored by 8.5 points. Daniels made his second start for Tampa Bay, replacing injured quarterback Baker
sports.content: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers beat the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 on Thursday night for their first win of the NFL season. Rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels led Tampa Bay with help from running back Bucky Irving. Dallas had been favored by 8.5 points. Daniels made his second start for Tampa Bay, replacing injured quarterback Baker Mayfield. Week 5 continues Sunday, Oct. 11, with 13 games, followed by Buffalo's visit to the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night. The Kansas City Chiefs and Carolina Panthers are on bye.
sports.image_alt: Buccaneers beat Cowboys 24-16 for first win of season

sports.title: India recalls Bhuvneshwar Kumar for New Zealand T20 series after four years
sports.summary: India has recalled fast bowler Bhuvneshwar Kumar to its T20 squad for the New Zealand tour, ending a four-year absence from the national side. Batting coach Sitanshu Kotak said the selectors likely valued Bhuvneshwar’s experience, his strong performances in the past two IPL seasons and his ability to bowl in New Zealan
sports.content: India has recalled fast bowler Bhuvneshwar Kumar to its T20 squad for the New Zealand tour, ending a four-year absence from the national side. Batting coach Sitanshu Kotak said the selectors likely valued Bhuvneshwar’s experience, his strong performances in the past two IPL seasons and his ability to bowl in New Zealand conditions. Kotak also pointed to the need for experienced bowling options when Jasprit Bumrah is absent and the squad includes young bowlers. Former India cricketer Deep Dasgupta questioned what the recall says about the country’s talent pipeline. India’s five-match series begins in Christchurch on October 22, with the final match scheduled for Hamilton on November 1.

sports.title: Brewers and Dodgers set NLCS rematch with pennant at stake

sports.content: The Milwaukee Brewers and Los Angeles Dodgers will meet in the National League Championship Series for a second straight year after both won their division series Wednesday. Milwaukee beat San Diego 3-1 in Game 4, and Los Angeles eliminated Atlanta in four games. Milwaukee, which set a franchise record with 103 regular-season wins, has home-field advantage against the 100-win Dodgers. The Brewers are seeking their first pennant since 1982, while Los Angeles is pursuing a third consecutive World Series title. Game 1 is scheduled for Sunday, October 11, at American Family Field in Milwaukee. The best-of-seven series will continue in Los Angeles before returning to Milwaukee for Games 6 and 7, if needed. The Dodgers swept Milwaukee in last year’s NLCS, but the Brewers won this season’s regular-season series 4-3. They are the National League’s two 100-win teams.

sports.content: Las Vegas Aces star A’ja Wilson won the 2026 WNBA Most Valuable Player award on Thursday, becoming the first player to win five MVPs and the first to win three in a row. She received 65 of 74 first-place votes and 713 points; Minnesota rookie Olivia Miles finished second with 442 points. Wilson averaged 26.2 points, 9.4 rebounds, 3.2 assists and 1.9 blocks in the regular season, leading the league in scoring for a third consecutive year. Her scoring average was the second-highest in WNBA history, behind her own 26.9 points per game in 2024. The defending champion Aces trail the Golden State Valkyries 2-0 in their best-of-five semifinal. Las Vegas faces elimination when it hosts Game 3 on Friday. Wilson said she would skip the planned trophy presentation to prepare with her team.

sports.content: India face West Indies in Ranchi on Friday in the second of five T20 internationals, seeking to extend their 1-0 series lead after an eight-wicket win in the opener. India chased the visitors’ 172 with 32 balls to spare as captain Shreyas Iyer scored an unbeaten 102 off 43 balls. The hosts’ main selection question is whether to retain opener Sanju Samson, who made 11 in the first match and has struggled in recent innings, or give 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi another chance. India have so far retained the Abhishek Sharma-Samson opening pairing, while Sooryavanshi impressed in practice in Ranchi. The match is scheduled to start at 7 p.m. local time.

sports.content: Carlos Alcaraz arrives at the Shanghai Masters feeling mentally fresh after winning the Japan Open, his first title since returning from a right-wrist injury that sidelined him from April until the US Open in August. He beat Jiri Lehecka 7-6 (7-4), 6-4 in Tuesday’s Tokyo final, but said his body is still adapting to the demands of competition. The world No. 3 also said tennis’s crowded calendar is pushing players too hard and that the sport is moving in the wrong direction as injuries mount. He has never progressed beyond the Shanghai quarter-finals and will begin in the second round. Alcaraz also said fellow player Holger Rune should give himself time as he returns from an Achilles injury, following the Dane’s early exits in Tokyo and Shanghai.

sports.content: New Zealand golfer Daniel Hillier hit a hole-in-one on the 17th hole at the Open de España in Madrid on Thursday, winning a BMW iX5. Hillier used an 8-iron for the 187-yard shot and was unhappy with his strike. Connor Syme, Grant Forrest and Spain’s Eugenio Chacarra shared the opening-round lead, with Sergio Garcia one shot behind. Chacarra played with a broken toe, while Ireland’s Shane Lowry opened with a one-under-par 70.

sports.summary: The Cleveland Guardians beat the Chicago White Sox 9-5 on Thursday in Chicago, tying their American League Division Series 2-2 after losing the first two games at home. sports.content: The Cleveland Guardians beat the Chicago White Sox 9-5 on Thursday in Chicago, tying their American League Division Series 2-2 after losing the first two games at home. The winner-take-all Game 5 is scheduled for Saturday, Oct. 10, at Progressive Field. The winner advances to face the Tampa Bay Rays in the AL Championship Series. Cleveland broke a 4-4 tie with six runs in the sixth inning. Travis Bazzana’s RBI double started the rally, and José Ramírez, Patrick Bailey, Chase DeLauter and Jo Adell followed with run-scoring hits. Adell’s single drove in two runs. Ramírez also hit a two-run homer in the fifth and finished with three RBIs, while Bailey added a home run. Starter Gavin Williams threw 18 pitches in relief to record the final three outs for Cleveland. Chicago reliever Grant Taylor, who allowed four runs without retiring a batter in the sixth, said he would be ready for any assignment in Game 5. Cleveland is seeking to become the first team since the 2017 Yankees to overcome a 2-0 deficit in a best-of-five postseason series.
